text_fidelity_a: H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat,Inflatable Paddle Board Universal/Adjustable/Detachable/Soft Padded Boat Seat and Backrest with Storage Bag for Fishing/Kayaking/ Rafting / Canoeing My wife and I recently got a H2OSUP and while my wife loves the SUP aspect, I have ankles that spent years of athletics and to that end, as I age, they don’t like standing on an SUP as much or as long. I saw this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat and grabbed it! I spend most of my time on SUPs seated in order to keep from growing pain. I am thrilled I grabbed it! Unfortunately, we haven’t been able to get on the water as we’d hoped. Now with winter bearing down... but we have tested out the SUPs and tried this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat on top - the H20 SUP products all seem to be - to our beginner knowledge - an excellent product line. So when I saw it was an H20 seat, I expected the same - I was right. The seat is well constructed of good materials, everything stitched and assembled well. Not having done this before (our tour SUPs never had seats) it was easy to fugue out how to put it together - attach - with common sense. Attach the clips to the 4 D Rings on the surface, and you’re ready to go. The seat is comfortable, holds well in place, and seems like it’ll give decent support. This is not a seat in that you can recline or that it’ll give you the same support as a chair. But with the attached straps that hold it in place, able to be adjusted for tension, you get a pretty decent amount of support while seated. I’m carrying a bit of extra weight, yet once seated and leaning back, I felt comfortable and like if I were on water, it would help me maintain comfort and help in supporting my back. In other words, I think it’ll work fine on the water. The seat is comfortable. I was wearing shorts, but I felt like I would be able to sit for a decent length of time and find it comfortable - not to mention be okay if I and the seat were wet. We are most likely to use these SUPs on salt water, so we plan to rinse them all off extensively with fresh water post-use in order to keep and maintain the integrity and longevity of the seat, SUP, and other supplies. In the end, my wife and I both feel like this H2OSUP Sit-On-Top Kayak Seat will turn our SUP into a great SUP-Kayak combination, and allow us more than one use and way to enjoy them. The H20 product line again seems like it’s quality and something we would consider getting again.

text_fidelity_a:
Smith & Wesson SWMP4LS 8.6in S.S. Assisted Folding Knife with 3.6in Serrated Clip Point Blade and Aluminum Handle for Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC , Black So I'll start by saying, I *love* the opening function of this knife. I have, and have had, other knives with the thumb post for "easy opening" but they never work as well as I had hoped. This thing is quick and opens fully every time with the slide button so I don't have to stop and put down whatever I have in my hand to pull out the knife and open it. It's also scary sharp new. I just hope that it will hold that edge through most everyday tasks and later, when needed, be easy to put that edge back on.
That said, this thing is a beast. It is both heavy and thick. I don't know if it is the internal mechanics causing both of these but it would be awesome if they could cut both the thickness and weight down by about 1/3. The heft in your hand is nice until that has been riding in your pocket all day.
All said it's still one of the best knives I've owned and anyone looking for a knife that is easy to open with one hand, should consider this.

Update 18 months later:
Still loving this knife. I have the $25 suction cup knife sharpener from Amazon and with that I have kept an edge on on this blade that shaves hair off my hand. Everyone who uses this thing comments on the knife and the sharpness. The mechanical opening of the blade can be a little much for some of my friends who are women, but they can open it manually so they still appreciate the knife in general. I still wish they could shave the size & weight of this down, but until that exists, this is the "opening assisted" knife to get.
text_fidelity_b: Smith & Wesson SWMP4LS 8.6in S.S. Assisted Folding Knife with 3.6in Serrated Clip Point Blade and Aluminum Handle for Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC , Black

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish I purchased this knife as a semi-impulse buy. I had been looking for a new edc for a couple months, however I was skeptic to stray away from my kershaw of 5 years.

After my initial purchase I read many mixed reviews, and after a month of carrying here are my thoughts.

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish

text_fidelity_a:
Ironman IFT 1000 Infrared Therapy Inversion Table This review is a commentary on my personal experience with Ironman IFT 1000; it is not a recommendation for treatment for any kind of physical ailment or injury. Please see your doctor.

Pertinent info: I'm a 5' 1", 150 lb. 65 year old woman with no other back/neck problems of which I'm aware.

I can't begin to tell you the pain I was in from a pinched nerve in my neck. For a week, I couldn't stand up for more than five minutes without my neck starting to burn and feel like someone was stabbing me. Bad enough that sometimes I really, really wanted to scream. I had to lie down on a small neck bolster with a heating pad on high to stop the pain, which took up to half a hour. Then I was stuck on my back until I was willing to endure the pain again. This was the seventh or eighth episode of this neck pain in the past couple of years, each episode worst than the last as to length and degree of pain. I missed seven days of work this time.

The success of the bolster/heat treatment is what led me to a self-diagnosis of a pinched nerve. You should see your doctor for diagnosis.

I first tried aTENS unit, which was a miserable failure for my particular condition. (I'm returning it to Amazon.) I ordered this inversion table and had friends assemble it for me since I absolutely couldn't do it. (Not nearly as simple as it looks like it should be.) I spent several hours up and down from bed making small adjustments to the unit until I had it right for me. (Tip, although I'm 5'1", the correct height setting for me on the boom arm turned out to be 5'7". I have the strap configured to allow the table to tilt no more than 35 to 40 degrees off the horizontal plane. This is FAR from completely inverted, which would be 90 degrees. However, when on the table, it feels like I'm close to upside-down.)

Once I had it adjusted to my satisfaction, I suspended myself for ten minutes, then waited to see how long it would take the pain to return while standing. 45 minutes! For someone who hadn't been able to eat anything in an upright position for a week, this was a miracle, and such a relief. Went back to bed for a couple of hours, then got back on the table again for 15 minutes. (I recommend sticking with a maximum of ten minutes as it states in the instructions.) I repeated this a couple of times in the next hour or so, sticking to ten minutes. Then I waited for the pain again. I went to bed for the night around three hours later with no pain. I woke up, got out of bed to see how long it would take the pain to hit again. When eight hours had passed and I was still pain free, I went ahead and used the table a couple of times during the remainder of the day as recommended in the instructions. That was yesterday and I'm still pain free and fixing to use the table for the first time today.

I plan on following the ten minutes, twice a day routine forever. I've read that inversion can reverse some of the damage gravity does to the internal organs over the years, compressing them and forcing them down out of their original positions. I'm hoping this will also help keep my heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, etc., from deteriorating.

I didn't buy this model for the heat function, but turns out it works just fine, at least on the first try. I'll probably not use it often, maybe in the winter to pamper myself sometimes. I'm pretty hot natured and additional heat isn't always comfortable for me. If the heat breaks, the table stays!

I'm impressed with the solid construction, the comfort of the ankle holders and the simplicity of the design. I would prefer more padding on the table, but that would probably interfere with the heat function. Attaching a piece of memory foam to the table somehow would probably work great if you don't care about the heat.

I must say that lifting my body forward to step down off the table is a little straining on my back, and someone with existing back issues might want someone else present to act as a "spotter " to aid in that, as well as to help with setting and releasing the ankle holders. You have to bend over at the waist to do that. To lean forward, I find it helps to bend my knees a little, which helps my hips act as a fulcrum. That makes it easier to lean forward to unlock the ankle holders and step off the table.

Please be aware that you may be slightly light headed when you return the table to it's upright position. Allow a few seconds for your head and inner ears to right themselves before you bend over to release the ankle holders. One final tip: If you have the slightest upset stomach, DON'T USE THE TABLE. Your stomach is likely to empty itself without warning - mine did. Probably best not to use the table on a full stomach, either. Gravity is a powerful force to move stomach contents the wrong direction, and the slight dizziness when returning to the upright position will exacerbate the problem.

I hope this review helps you make your purchasing decision.
text_fidelity_b: Ironman IFT 1000 Infrared Therapy Inversion Table

SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes I ordered two Sunlite (Kenda) Thorn resistant tubes (700c x 18/23) with removable presta core in July of 2015. I wanted a thick (puncture resistant) tube that allowed me to remove the core (with a chain tool) to allow me to inject tire sealant into the tube.

In the Southwest, we have nasty thorns called 'goatheads' that cause many flats. As part of my defense system, I use: 1) a thick, thorn resistant tube, 2) tire sealant (Flat Attack); 3) a high-quality, super puncture-resistant tire (Schwalbe - Marathon Plus Tour, Marathon Supreme, or Durano Plus - depending on the bike).

I waited a while to see how these Sunlite tubes would hold up. Unfortunately, after about a year and a half, the front tube failed. The presta valve stem separated from the tube, rendering the tube unrepairable and useless. The rear tube got a flat, but due to the tire sealant, I was able to simply pump up the tire, spin the wheel, and it sealed itself.

I had high hopes for these tubes, but I will look for other alternatives.

TIP: One reason that many of these tubes may be failing at the stem is due to the threaded, round 'nut' on the valve stem. The nut is really helpful when inflating the tube for the FIRST time, (i.e., when there is no air in it). However, once inflated to full pressure, I would recommend REMOVING this nut and setting it aside. The problem is that when riding with this nut tightened down on the valve stem, it creates added pressure on the stem at the base of the tube, increasing the likelihood of separation & failure.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes

Bobby Jones Golf Apparel - Performance Optimum Flex-Lite Polyester/Spandex Moisture-Wicking Sport Shorts for Men These shorts are made of 90% polyester and 10% spandex. They certainly feel like polyester with that slick slinky look and feel. The spandex gives them some firms stretch. But there is little to no stretch in the waist.

I have the size 36. They measure 21 inches from the top to the bottom. The inseam measures 10 inches. The listed as thirty-six, they really are about 38 inches in the waist. There is a plastic zipper with a button on top. I don’t really know what this part is called, but it is the inside flap behind the zipper. It’s way too wide. So it even arrived folded over. It’s just annoying. The waist has the name “Bobby Jones” written all around the inside and silicone. This helps the shorts stay in place. There are nice deep pockets on the side. Two back pockets, but no buttons on the back pockets.

These shorts are made in Thailand. At the current price of 100 bucks they are at least eighty bucks overpriced. It’s understandable that you pay a premium for a brand name, but paying 100 bucks for shorts that could not have cost more than five bucks to make in Thailand is just outrageous.

I was concerned about the electronic finger print scanner dying and then not being able to access the contents. There’s a small USB charging port on the keypad area. There is also a key hole on the front.

The app (search billconch) is fair simple to navigate. Within 5 minutes I had two finger prints stored. The app also shows how much battery is left.

Inside the safe is a LED light that automatically is triggered when the safe pops open. The bottom of the safe is lined with a removable piece of foam padding.

If I were have to name something I don’t like about the safe... I appears pretty heavy. But I guess that’s not a bad thing?

text_fidelity_a:
Kizer Cutlery C01C 3.25" Flipper Titanium Stonewash Plain Flooding Knife, Blue I ordered this knife not only because of its style but also because of how rugged it looked. As a knife collector my leaning is toward the larger and stronger knives that I could rely upon for a long time should the need arise. Even if that need never comes up, I enjoy having a collection of good looking blades at hand.

The knife came wrapped in a plastic sleeve which was inside a zippered camo bag and packaged in a reinforced box. Also included was a polishing cloth and a warranty pamphlet. The knife is guaranteed against defects in material and workmanship and has a limited lifetime warranty to the original owner.

Now on to the knife itself. I paid the vendor $184.44 and expected to get the blue knife as shown in the picture on the product page. Unfortunately the knife was delivered in the standard steel grey color with the only blue color being on the accent ring on the ball bearing pivot. Aside from the missing color, this is one well-made and smoothly functioning flipper. The titanium handle fills your hands and the 3.25" blade is a thick and well finished CPM-535VN stainless steel.

This thing locks up tighter than a bank vault and lends credence to the company's reputation for tight tolerances and great quality. There is absolutely no blade wobble when the blade is extended and releasing the frame lock is easily and smoothly done. The blade came sharp enough to cut paper and also shave the hair on the back of my hand. It could be made sharper though without comprising the integrity of the blade.

My husband built me a tetherball pole/base as the reviews on standard ones just didn't cut it. However, the base is not a concern in this review.

We've only played with the tetherball a total of 3 times. First time was fine (it was also the very first time my husband had actually played thetherball). But the second time when I played with a friend, the rope from the pole to the ball tore right at the base of the ball. I thought "no big deal I'll just tie it back on"

False. I tied it back on and within 30 minutes, it tore off again. I added on several knots and even went to YouTube to look up sturdy knots but that's not the issue. The string for this ball is VERY flimsy and weak.

On the third go around, the ball came flying off mid-serve and could have injured someone. Ball itself seems to be fine and sturdy. The rope itself, again, is just crappy overall. It keeps breaking and it's not easy to "re-string", if you will.

Overall, the ball is great and seems to be sturdy. However, if you're a grown adult looking into smacking the heck out of a tetherball, definitely be prepared to get a new, sturdier rope because the one that comes with it just doesn't cut it.

JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control Speed
For aggressive players, this paddle comes up a little short. The weight of the paddle makes it seem like it's a heavy hitter, but the added rubber absorbs some of the energy so you lose power. Overall, you'll still get some great power shots but it won't improve your speed.

Spin
The spin on this paddle is very good and easy to produce. Right out of the package, you can tell the rubber is well made and has good traction. I was able to get good back/top/side spin without too much effort. In comparison to other Joola rackets I've owned, the spin is fairly good but it lacks some spin traction that I would expect. If you're coming from a basic racket (i.e. the cheap ones you see at discount stores) the spin on this paddle increase your spin game greatly.

Control
This is one area I felt this paddle excelled in. The grip, the 5-Ply real wood, the padding, everything about this paddle makes playing really easy. For someone who is getting more serious about their game, the added control to this racket is perfect. The control aspect of the racket is well balanced which can aid in improving your spin and attacks.

Overview
The Joola Infinity Balance Racket is well made recreational racket that is great for the enthusiast. The racket is decently padded for control and has decent spin capabilities. It's perfect for someone who isn't perfecting a particular playing style but just loves to play table tennis. It's very well balanced, feels great in the hand and had some decent power and spin.

NATHAN Running Belt Waist Pack 5K with Reflective Detail, Zippers and Adjustable Pouch Strap - Runners Fanny Pack - Bounce Free Pouch, Ultra-Lightweight Neoprene - Fits all Phones (iPhone, Android, Windows) - For Men and Women - Running, Biking, Hiking, CrossFit, Workout I got back into distance running just after one of my kids was diagnosed with a chronic illness so once I started running beyond 2 miles, I felt I had to have my cell phone to stay in touch with my wife. I've gone through multiple packs and armbands for phones, gels, etc. My previous Fuel Belt and SPi Belts were ok but not spectacular.

When I gave up on iPhones a week ago, I opted for a much larger Samsung Galaxy S4 Active and topped it off with an Otterbox case. I immediately realized NONE of my belts/packs were going to hold the phone. Out of desperation, I ran over to Dick's Sporting Goods to see what was available. I couldn't believe my luck when they had the Nathan 5k and another belt, by Nike, that also fit my phone. The Nathan was the clear winner, though, because it had a wider, softer material for it's belt and it also was stretchier.

I have not regretted my decision! Despite having a giant hunk of a phone, I can't even feel this thing when I wear it. And it doesn't rub in the slightest. They only way I know it's there is I occasionally hear the zippers jingling a little. It easily holds my phone, house key, and gels.

I did say there was a flaw. It's minor but it's a real head scratcher. They belt includes enough material strap this belt to Andre the Giant's larger brother! And there's no loop to hold it. Unlike many other belts, the belt part itself doesn't loop back on itself, adjusted by buckles. Instead, it just cinches like an ordinary belt. I've got a 34 waist and there's probably at least a foot of excess belt strap. But I've tucked it in for the relatively short runs I've run so far and used a rubber band on a longer one. I'll cut it eventually but hadn't b/c I wanted to make sure I wasn't missing a piece. Other reviews echo my concern, so I guess not.

But overall (believe it or not), the best belt you can buy!

text_fidelity_a:
Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange This is a great way to carry extra ammo for your concealed carry weapon. They are easy to load, lie flat in your pocket, and easy to take out when reloading. It sure beats using a bulky speed loader. Yes, the speed loader is quicker, but your chances of needing more than eight shots to defend yourself is minimal.

Eight shots you ask? I bit the bullet (so to speak) and purchased a Smith and Wesson .357 Magnum Model 327 Performance Center, an eight shot revolver. It is a scandium snub nose that holds .38 specials, 38 + P, and .357 magnums. Light but bulky, it fits my large hands well and the recoil (even under full magnum loads) is manageable. Expensive but unique, it is a gun that will become a collector item in the future. Not many revolvers can hold eight large bullets.

And yes, it is a wheel gun for personal protection. My first gun purchase 41 years ago was a Ruger Blackhawk in .44 magnum, carried while salmon fishing in Alaska. I also own a Smith and Wesson .44 magnum Alaskan, another snub nose revolver. So recoil isn't an issue for me. Why a revolver instead of one of the excellent semi autos out there? If I ever need to use it to protect myself or my family, I need to know that it will go BANG when I pull the trigger. I also need to know that my spouse can use it without fumbling around.. Just aim it and pull the trigger. And then again, and again. The simplicity and "bullet proof" action inspires confidence -- especially when you find yourself in a very stressful situation.

My backup piece is also a revolver that will handle the same three calibers. Just in case. Kinda like wearing a belt and suspenders. Redundancy is not a bad thing in personal protection.
text_fidelity_b: Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange

text_fidelity_a: SPRI Women's Fitness Gloves I have been lifting weight for over 30 years and have used many different types, styles, and brands of gloves. It is a great sport for the body, but very hard on the hands. Gripping and lifting iron weights can cause major calluses across the palm of your hands. They hurt and look unsightly at the same time. Weight lifting gloves can minimize or eliminate the possibility of getting painful calluses. I had never heard of SPRI FITNESS GLOVES, but was very excited to give them a try. At first glance the look and styling is very sharp with the black glove with the simple red accent color. I usually wear leather work-out gloves and these are made from a foam/rubber material.  I am not crazy about the smell. They have a wide Velcro strap across the top of the hand that makes it easy to get them on and off, but I find it unusual to have that strap on top of the hand instead of on top of the wrist. I’m not sure if it was uncomfortable or if I am so used to having gloves that secured around my wrist.  I also like the support that you get from having gloves that close over the wrist, which these do not. They appear to be cheaply made in that the finger-tips look like they were cut off with a pair of scissors. The quality, material, and the fit are not to my satisfaction, not to mention the smell. They might break-in with repeated use, but I want a glove that is comfortable, functional, and fits well the first time I put them on.  On top of everything else. . . They are Made in China and a bit expensive.

text_fidelity_a:
Workout Logbook for Women & Men; Mother's Day Gift; 90 Day Fitness Planner & Tracker; Journal; Gym Journal; Gym Logbook; Fitness Diary; Exercise Journal; Gift for Athletes; Athletes's Journal Following a few injuries my wife and I are getting back to our workouts, but wanted to get some bigger steps this time and specific outcomes, so we decided to grab some journals. I had gotten one that leans on more of a weight-centric program. My wife is more mixed between cardio and weights, so I thought this one might be of help. In the end, this is an okay, not good nor great journal, but will do something to at least let her track. She will use it, but we agree, it is not the best option for anyone beyond a beginner starting out.

1. It is made from decent materials with a hard cardboard front and back to give stability when working inside. The binding is spiral, allowing it to fully open and not bunch up the pages. From this aspect, it is well done.

2. The options within are more limited than mine and others we have looked at.

A. The introduction of Why is pretty basic, but good for beginners, but limited for those beyond.

B. There are places to track your weight and body shape changes at the beginning, 30 day, 60 day, and 90 day marks. There are no spots for doing so between, which in my expense and from my reading, one should not track weight and other elements daily. Some suggest weekly or monthly. In this case, it is monthly (every 30 days). My journal offers weekly tracking with more options on WHAT to track and HOW to do it. I think this is notable in that while mine and this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker tracks the same elements of the body, mine provides little diagrams of WHERE on the body these points lie. As I think this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is lacking this information, which if geared towards beginners, would be helpful information.

C. My journal offers far more options on all of these aspects across the board. For example, mine has space for 13 exercises per page and Sets 1 - 6 whereas this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker has it strangely set up in Sets 1 - 5 with Weight and Reps. It's as if they see a Set as an exercise and think you are doing five exercises. At least that's how we are reading it. Then you put in how many reps. in each set.

D. Things like Water intake in this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker are just a question: Water Intake? In mine (and others) they tend to have a way to track, such as something open you fill in when you have a glass or something you check off. I prefer such a way in that you tick it off with each one as opposed to this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker which is answering a question - "5." Now you're having to keep track to fill it out. YES, you can certainly check off or make tick marks - but that really should be set up in the design.

E. Little things like tracking what area of the body or muscles you worked (legs, core, back, etc) are NOT included here which is a shame. But they do include things like "Next session modifications and/focus"... not even sure what that would mean - I THINK it's their way of having you in fact track if you did core, legs, chest, etc. The space available for these question answers is pretty limited.

F. Another reviewer noted there are "Examples" provided in some pages but are printed on the lines and you have to write over it. It is true how they printed it and it's kind of annoying. Why would I want to keep writing over it?

G. While not as bad in the wording and grammar of many products made in China, there are some obvious (glaring) strange parts. Nothing one cannot workout and that make this a bad book, but they are notable.

In the end, this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is okay and would be fine for many beginners looking to workout and track that journey for the first 90 days. It is not in your face, it is a way to learn and pace yourself and and get the information down. I don't think it's all that bad that it would be with a 1 or 2 star rating, but certainly does not earn 4 or 5. In the end I went with 3 because it is workable, easy to use and write in, and it does provide elements one wishes to track when getting into a practice. That said, there are much better options on the market, even for beginners, and I would personally look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Workout Logbook for Women & Men; Mother's Day Gift; 90 Day Fitness Planner & Tracker; Journal; Gym Journal; Gym Logbook; Fitness Diary; Exercise Journal; Gift for Athletes; Athletes's Journal

SANLIKE Fishing Reel Baitcasting Reel for Saltwater Freshwater, Magnet Dual Braking Force Bait Casting Reel, Ultra Smooth 17.6 Lb Carbon Fiber Drag - 6.3:1 Gear Ratio - Right Hand I know the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel is advertised for salt water foremost...but I can't see it. To my way of thinking it's more of a lightweight bass reel. And it is light and small of frame. Two hours after I got mine I was on a local public lake trying it out. Been looking forward to it.

Size-wise it would be at home on a lighter rod if that's your notion. I mated mine to an old comfy Speed Stick. First thing I noticed was the spool isn't solid. It has holes in it. I'm sure there is a more scientific way to say it but I don't know what it is. A small matter, but it makes tying the line onto it much easier, as you can pass it through the holes. Next up, something I haven't seen before...the drag 'clicks' as you adjust it. An improvement, I think, as it gives more finesse to the operation. Otherwise the reel behaves much as any other.

I have a ton of reels. Some mine, some hand-me-downs. Some are top o' the line too. But one thing I have noticed...high dollar or low dollar they ALL wear out just the same. Point being that since this is the case for the money, you can't do better with high dollar than you can with the SAN Like Baitcasting Fishing Reel. If you're just starting out you can purchase 3 or 4 for less than you'll spend on one of the big names. Functionally there isn't much difference and like I said, they all have a lifespan. Heck, rod and reel makers could give away their products to sell their branded lures. That's where all your money is going anyway.

One tip. The brake knob. On power casts with mine time and again at the apex I'd get that professional overlap thing. My reel, at any rate, is pretty finicky about having enough resistance. Typically you set that knob so your bait drops slowly and that's it. But this reel needs a bit more braking... then it works like a charm. So if you get a tangle, just run that knob up a bit more. You'll still be able to get that bait way out there without the birds nest effect.

Only time and use will tell how my new reel holds up, but for my money, I'm tickled with it. It's as much as I hoped for and nary a complaint. I'd love to see some validation with good reviews.
text_fidelity_b: SANLIKE Fishing Reel Baitcasting Reel for Saltwater Freshwater, Magnet Dual Braking Force Bait Casting Reel, Ultra Smooth 17.6 Lb Carbon Fiber Drag - 6.3:1 Gear Ratio - Right Hand

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued) Like many others, I researched this bike for about 2 weeks before deciding to purchase it. I read everything I could find about Schwinn bikes period. The model before this (the 130) is what I was going to purchase at WalMart, it was cheaper but I would have to pay for tax & shipping (free shipping and no tax on Amazon.com) so it was only going to save me about $30 at WalMart (for the older model) so I am definitely glad I decided to buy the 140 at Amazon.com.
The previous model (130) was highly rated/recommended on the Consumer Report websites and that made me realize that a newer model would/should be even better. I live in a small apartment and although I wanted the recumbent one, I had to go with the upright. Not to mention, I figured I could work on my posture while riding upright. (ha ha) This bike is just what I need to get in shape. I have a leg injury and I am overweight and out of shape. I needed a piece of equipment that I could commit to and not feel like I was doing a dreaded chore. I can hop on this bike and watch tv, listen to music, talk with people around me, or just look out of my window.

At first I felt like the price was expensive compared to the other models, but it's true, you get what you pay for. As I mentioned, I am overweight and I needed something that would last while I pursued my fitness goals. The other brands are not built as well as the Schwinn models. Simply look at the frame work and tubing and you can tell.
After I put it together (without any problems whatsosever) I realized that it was of good quality and worth the money I spent. The setup was easy. I am a female with manicured nails and I didn't even chip my polish putting this bike together. I also didn't require any help. It was really easy. I had my laptop on my sofa with the manual enlarged (I went to the Schwinn website and downloaded it) so that I could see the images clearly, but I mainly used the paper manual that the bike came with.

I read the instructions for the setup of the user profile and everything went just fine.
~I read some reviews about little issues with customizing, but if you just take your time and read the manual, you will really see its not difficult. When you set up a custom workout, you have to realize that it goes through 30 levels so it appears as though nothing is happening, but be patient as you customize it and you will see that it is working right.~
~Also the Heart Rate monitor, if you simply plug it in on the side, it should work just fine. You just have to look for the spot to plug it in to.~
I have only used the bike 4 times so I can't give you any long term use information, other than the programs are nice, the resistance is great, and it has a lot of features on the console once you set up your user profile, but I can say that this is a very good investment for anyone considering purchasing a quality exercise bike. It is a good piece of equipment. If you have to save up a little to get the bike, start saving! If you are considering a different brand, forget about it! If you think that its hard to put together, get over the thought! If you are worried about it not being right for you, try it and you will like it!

I have a lot of weight to lose and I don't like going to the gym. I walk around my neighborhood which is ok, but now I can get a good little cardio workout. I am so glad that I got this bike. I am helping myself in the long run. This is the best way to spend over $300 and have something well worth it!

No missing/broken pieces, no damaged stabilizers, no damaged or flimsy box. I ordered and received in exactly 7 days. ***I'm NOT discrediting anyone's reviews about problems they had with their purchase, I am just stating that my purchase was problem free***

~I will add another review/or update in the future about how the bike is performing~ I hope this helps motivate someone!
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued)

Swim Caps Ear Protection 3D - Swimming Cap for Women Men - Silicone Swim Cap Waterproof - Fits Long Hair & Short - Adult Swim Cap - Youth Swim Cap - Swim Hats I SO wanted this cap to work out. I swim laps a pool using a snorkel mask. Maybe that's what compromised the seal? I have no idea, but the cap seemed to fit snug enough when I first put it on. I had no lotion on my face or slippery stuff to loosen the cap. It felt VERY comfy on my child-sized head.

But. Minutes into my 40-min lap swim in the pool, I could feel water sloshing around my ears! I had earplugs in JUST IN CASE - but in no way do the flush design of the earplugs get in the way. My TYR earplugs fit in my ear canal with NO stick poking out.

Bugged, I kept swimming anyway. After my swim, I removed my cap and sure enough, a cup o'water poured out of the cap! The ear cups on this cap seem to HOLD water inside, and the seal on the cap appears not to be strong enough to keep water out. Again, it *could* be due to the snorkel mask and strap I had on, but really? I did better with a traditional swim cap with NO molded ears on it.

SO GLAD I kept my TYR earplugs IN, cuz that kept the pool water out of my ear canals. It would've been really gross to have that cup of pool water flushing IN and OUT of my ear canals for 40 min.
text_fidelity_b: Swim Caps Ear Protection 3D - Swimming Cap for Women Men - Silicone Swim Cap Waterproof - Fits Long Hair & Short - Adult Swim Cap - Youth Swim Cap - Swim Hats

text_fidelity_a:
M-Wave Bicycle Cycling Bag Since three vastly different items are in one listing: This is for the individual panniers. They seem solid enough. A bit of a loose seam or thread here or there, seen a lot worse. They have a good bit of space inside, I reckon 3 2-liter soda bottles a side with some stuff along the sides, but it'll be wonky because of the round bottom. The design of the top makes them water resistant, it's not a zipper. The stiffening material is thicker than I expected, will definitely provide protection and support for fairly heavy items. The clips and D-rings don't feel cheap or fragile.

The problems:

I ordered two and got two left-side panniers instead of a matched pair. I didn't even IMAGINE this would be a problem. Title, bullet points and description all need to say "left side only" if that's what it is, AND THE RIGHT SIDE OPTION NEEDS TO BE IN THE SAME LISTING. In any case I don't think heel striking will be a problem, they just look weird.

The top clips are sized for rails no more than 9mm(based on the diameter of the inner clearing, measured by caliper) while the side rails on an Ibera Touring Carrier Plus are 10.5mm. So it only clips on with the first clearing, not very strongly. They also come contracted shut- I had to stretch them out by putting 11.5mm thick pens in each one and leaving them overnight(see attached image.) Now I can at least get the clips on over the rail.

The next problem is that the Ibera rack has no good place to hook the stabilizing bungee. I will need to hook it somewhere weird, which means the panniers can't be taken off with one hand which is a disappointment.

I will try them a couple of times carrying groceries, the purpose I got them for. Their fate is up to how well they do the job.
text_fidelity_b: M-Wave Bicycle Cycling Bag

text_fidelity_a: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock Great lock for securing secondary components like seat and front wheel on your bike.  I live in Baltimore where bike theft is an issue, but not as bad as it is in bigger cities.  The general recommendations are U-Lock your frame and rear wheel first, then secure the front wheel and seat with something like a cable or chain lock.  I needed this longer length chain to secure my seat, and I use the shorter Abus steel chain lock to secure my front wheel to the frame.  This may be a little bit of overkill, but it is not unusual in Baltimore to see locked up bikes with the front wheel missing, and I overheard a woman in my LBS who was coming in to buy a new seat because hers had just been stolen.  These things can/do happen, and the harder you make it for thieves, the more likely the thieves are to pass you by for an easier target.  Seats and quick-release wheels are easy to steal when left unsecured, and they are expensive to replace.  A cable lock costs about as much, but is significantly easier to defeat than these chain locks.  I like these Abus locks (this one and the shorter one) because they are a small investment for a lot of peace of mind.
text_fidelity_b: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock

There is no information to show if this water bottle is dishwasher safe or not. But usually with bottles like this. . . even through they are plastic. .. It’s better to hand-wash because at the very least the writing on the outside will probably come off if you place it into the dishwasher. A bottle brush will be needed, and that too will need to be purchased separately, if you don’t already have one.

This water bottle does not have a “locking lid”, per-se. But there is a cap that covers over the mouthpiece when closed. There is a silicone strip around the top to make it easier to unscrew.

TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641 I have gone back to a wheel gun for concealed carry because I can't afford the one time that I might need to use my defensive weapon and have it jam. I know, I know! The modern semi autos are basically fool proof and malfunctions only happen occasionally. And I know that even with a subcompact you can easily carry 8-10 rounds of whatever, but I learned a long time ago that the more moving parts in any machine/tool, the more potential problems can happen -- and usually at the worst possible time. (Thank you Mr. Murphy).

My new defensive carry is a Smith & Wesson Model 327 2" Performance Center that holds eight rounds of 38 Special/ 38 +P/357 Magnum. It is a rather large revolver made of scandium and has a large grip which fits my hand perfectly. I'm a big guy so it's really no problem to conceal and the 2" barrel should make it qualify (in court) as a defensive weapon should I have to use it. My backup is a Ruger LCR in 357, a light and tiny gun that is a devil to shoot full power loads in. Fortunately I'm a big fan of 44 magnums and am comfortable handling a lot of recoil. Why the Ruger LCR as backup? There's nothing like redundancy in personal defense. A second gun using the same ammo covers most of the bases.

The result is that I can carry two revolvers loaded with a total of 13 rounds -- equaling or surpassing any of the subcompact/compact autos -- that will both go "Bang" when needed. And, and this is a big "And", any family member or passerby will also be able to operate either one of them should I be in trouble/incapacitated. All you have to do is pull the trigger. The alternative is a semi auto that might pose operating difficulty to whomever tries to be of assistance. There won't be enough time to lecture anyone on the operating mechanics of a semi auto.

So I picked up two QuickStrips and this pouch. Putting in two of the strips, one facing up and one facing down, creates a relatively slim package holding an additional ten rounds -- on top of the thirteen already loaded in the two revolvers. The total of 23 rounds should be enough for 99% of the potential situations encountered in most areas. I try to keep myself out of dangerous areas/predicaments (situational awareness), but if I have to enter one I will have a Glock 19 as my backup. A good man knows his limitations.
text_fidelity_b: TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641

DONNGYZ Underwater Submersible Diving Scuba Cylinder Oxygen Tank 0.5L & 4500PSI High Pressure Pump Adapter+Case(US Stock) While the quality did appear good the scuba shops will not touch them as they do not have the Stamp required for a fill.
This was not shared at time of purchase for the manufacturer and the information packet with the unit is almost non existent leaving you to figure it out yourself!
They supply you with replacement parts which is great and like I said its build decently but they expect the buyer to know the whole unit without directions!
I did need to put the unit together and find out what the torque specs are on something like this and had to tighten the gauge on it a couple of times to stop air leaks. The pump is a good quality and the tank is good quality but the Chinese manufacturer chose the easy route and did not meet Osha guidelines. So in closing the tank is only useful for very short submersions like untangling a boat prop or simple underwater inspections that take 5 to 10 minutes tops. Better off having an 80 tank to fill the smaller tank with as it takes much less time. I ended up buying a 40 with harness to use with my regulator to keep on the boat for a more reliable 25 minute submersion. So buyer beware its good but its not what you might expect!
text_fidelity_b: DONNGYZ Underwater Submersible Diving Scuba Cylinder Oxygen Tank 0.5L & 4500PSI High Pressure Pump Adapter+Case(US Stock)
